why: Measure current authored-cast gameplay with process memory observations rather than retired creator-cache counters.
scope: Established Caatinga public-playthrough checkpoint, five authored residents, twelve mixed buildings, 1440x900 headless Chromium, four reset 60-second still/panning preferred 1x/diagnostic16x phases.
verdict: observations complete; desktop hardware performance and long plateau unproven
limits: SwiftShader software renderer, not Metal desktop baseline.
RSS includes shared pages; process RSS totals are not unique allocations. GPU process host RSS is not GPU allocation/VRAM.
Renderer RSS grows over loading/phase resets and final samples vary. Four reset minutes cannot prove long-run plateau.
JavaScript performance.memory samples are constant/quantized here and cannot prove heap stability.
1x phases include automatic 16x intervals; no pure 1x throughput claim.
Developer import/forced-speed fixture, not public authoring or speed-control evidence.
